utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I'm sorry that because of a matter which delayed me we are late starting. We are told that there may be some procedural matters to be raised. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. In the course of the re-examination of Professor Taseva, the professor was shown two documents, which the Defence would like to tender into evidence. I have shown both of the documents to my learned friends from the Prosecution, and it is my understanding that they will not have any objections to the admission. The first document is 65 ter 1D1268. This document is actually the Law on Special Rights of the Members of the Security Services of the Republic of Macedonia and members of their families, which defines the security forces and what they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Prosecution has no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be received, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D313, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second document that the Defence would like to tender for admission is 65 ter 1DP29 [as interpreted] which was shown to Professor Taseva in re-examination. This is a combat order that was issued by the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia on the 21st of June, 2001 and sent to the unit for special tasks of the Ministry of Interior. It seems that the number has been recorded wrongly. I shall repeat it, Your Honour. 65 ter 1D529.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received by consent.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D314, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, finally, Your Honour, I would kindly ask for document P96 to be admitted with part of the translation of the article, starting from Article 286 to 296. Your Honour, in keeping with your previous decision, large documents have not always been translated fully, and it has been suggested that the parties that wish to use parts that have not been translated at the moment when the document was admitted to do their own translation. This is one part of the document, P96 which speaks about the use and possession of arms. This was admitted --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the counsel could repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the identification number of this document, which the Defence has been given from the CLSS service, and at our request the CLSS has translated this part of the Exhibit P96. We would kindly ask for this part of the translation to be joined with the Exhibit P96.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So it's merely to add a translation of part of the existing exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Which was previously not translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That translation will be added to the existing exhibit, P96.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Clerk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm afraid there are two more matters which we would like to bring to the attention of the Chamber at this stage. Two of the issues which were scheduled or put on the agenda for this afternoon have been resolved and I'm grateful to my colleague. Your Honour. The first one related to the Rule 92 bis summaries of four witness statements and the proposition of the Defence would be perhaps to read those statement for the record later in the week when there is a break, for instance between two witnesses as it might be more efficient. The second issue which was listed on the agenda concerned two documents, Your Honour, which we have placed on the list of documents to be used with the next witness, Mr. Keskovski. Those documents do not appear on our Rule 65 ter lists and we should formally seek leave to add them to our list before tendering them and we have indicated to our colleagues that we believe the best way to do so would be to seek leave at the time when the document is being shown and used with the witness rather than at the commencement of the hearing. If it is agreeable to the Chamber, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if counsel are agreed it will be more practical the matter can be dealt document by document as you reach it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Your Honour, the third matter which we would like to bring to your attention concerned an application for the admission of a number of document from the bar table by the Defence and more specifically to a response to that motion dated the 14th of February of 2008. It concerns the general motion for admission of documents from the bar table as opposed to the one that relates to the, quote, unquote, armed conflict motion. The Defence would seek leave, Your Honour, briefly to reply to a matter but before we do so we would like to indicate that we are well out of time to reply to the matter and that the basis for our request, Your Honour, is simply that we have reviewed a number of correspondence between the Prosecution and ourselves and that we would wish to bring to the attention of the Chamber a particular exchange in relation to this issue which we should in frankness have done within the deadline for the reply. At this stage, Your Honour, we simply seek leave in the belief that this clarification or this addition may assist the Chamber in its consideration of this matter, if permitted to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, as my colleague has indicated, the Defence are well out of time. Second of all, the Chamber has indicated that they only wish to receive replies at this stage of the proceedings when there really are exceptional circumstances warranting a reply and I haven't heard really from my colleague that he has established or described such circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps to specify, I don't want to be unfair to my colleague by going into the substance but perhaps to explain at least before you decide whether to allow us to proceed, the Prosecution made certain submissions in relation to an intercept of a particular conversation which was played to a witness, and in its response the Prosecution refers to a position which it says the Defence took in relation to this matter. In effect, Your Honour, there was an e-mail in response to the e-mail to which the Prosecution refers and we believe that this response that we gave to the Prosecution at the time could assist the Chamber in its determination and would certainly be of assistance to understand the position in this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will not receive the document, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be all for the procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything of yours, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I have a procedural issue, but I would ask the counsel that this be done in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just looking ahead a little further, Mr. Apostolski, the prospect is now seen that the Boskoski Defence will finish on Monday of next week. Are you in a position to continue from that point on? Perhaps starting Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence of Johan Tarculovski is prepared to begin its Defence on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We notice that you are continuing to be very careful in your scrutiny of potential witnesses and reducing your case even more as matters are dealt with here. How would you see the length of your case at the present time, Mr. Apostolski? Is it too early yet to get a prediction?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as for the length of the case, perhaps it is a little bit too earlier for me to say. I believe that we will be within the foreseen time-frame. It may even be reduced because we have stricken some of the witnesses off the list, and most probably Witness M2D-007 will most probably also be stricken off the list, and we anticipate the Defence of Johan Tarculovski would take about 15 working days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That would make it very touch-and-go, if you understand that expression, to finish by at least one of the Easters, not the orthodox Easter but the other Easter. That would probably be around 12 or 13 days, rather than 15. Is it practical, do you think, to think of finishing the evidence by that Easter, which would be Thursday, the 20th of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can say that there is a slight possibility to that end, but I cannot state with certainty at this moment. It would depend on how the testimony transpires. We feel that most of the time will be used to question the military expert. I believe that his will be the longest testimony and the others will -- will take less time than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, maybe you're inviting the Chamber to be very determined in its scrutiny of times, and if we do that it may be possible to finish everything by Easter. We will accept that challenge, Mr. Tarculovski -- Mr. Apostolski. I keep doing that. But I think your client has got used to it. And we will see if that is feasible. Of course we're not wanting to shorten your case to the point where the case is adversely affected, but if just by careful management of time we can finish by Easter it would be to everyone's advantage in terms of reaching the actual end of the case. Because I'm sure that your two clients, above all else, are now at the point where they would dearly love to see the end of this case. Very well. Thank you for that. Is there any issue that you --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise but I just want to note that I will take into consideration and -- what you have said and I will try to adjust my pace to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We've grateful. Is there any comment you would want to make, Mr. Saxon, in all of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps we may now have the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please take the card that is given to you and read aloud the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Mettraux has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. For the record my name is Guenael Mettraux and I'm appearing together with Edina Residovic on behalf of Mr. Boskoski. Could you state your name, date and place of birth for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: My name is Zlatko Keskovski. I was born on 29 June, 1970 in Ohrid, the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you married, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I have two small children, Aleksander and Vladimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you state briefly what your current professional occupation is. What is your job?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm a lecturer in martial arts at the university Fon at the faculty of security and detectives in Skopje, the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, briefly, could you state in summary at least what your education is, what your educational background is?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I am an a mechanical engineer and a marketing manager at public management.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And where did you receive those degrees from, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I graduated at the faculty of mechanical engineering in Bitola, Republic of Macedonia, and a college in Novi Sad, Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And aside from your professional activities, do you have any extra-curricular activities which are to be mentioned here? In particular, are you engaged in any sort of society or organisation?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm a member of the board of directors of the World Karate Association with headquarters in Italy; I'm a representative of kendai [phoen], the federation for the Republic of Macedonia and one of its founders. I am a founder and a representative for Macedonia for the Jiu-Jitsu federation for Macedonia, official representatives for the Japanese karate federation for the Republic of Macedonia. I conduct training of various security groupations of civilian nature, and I have done so through many European countries and throughout the world, starting as of 1994 onwards. I am the only Balkan instructor of karate for people with disabilities and I hope there will be many other things that will follow. I am also a four-time world champion in Jiu-Jitsu, third in the world in 1997, champion in New York, 1996. I have received the medal of Saint Kliment from the town of Ohrid, three medals for fostering the karate sport in Macedonia, certificate of gratitude from the organisation for people with disabilities of the city of Skopje, and a certificate of appreciation from the home for children without parents from Skopje, a former engagement with these children and many other such awards.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, just a quick point of clarification. You've indicated that you have conducted training for what is translated as security groupations of civilian nature. Does this include law enforcement organisation, police forces abroad?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I've conducted training of instructors who train various security structures in a number of European countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And going backward, perhaps, a bit in your career, did you at some stage join of Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you indicate when that was and in what capacity you joined?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I became employed at the Ministry of Interior officially in 1999. My first post was head of section for the security of the president of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We're going to come back to your employment and your activities in the sector of security of the president. But could you tell me whether at some stage you left the security sector of the president, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I left the security sector of the president of the Republic of Macedonia on the 1st of June, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware, Mr. Keskovski, of a number of stories or rumours which were published in the Macedonian press about the reason for your departure from this position? Are you aware of those stories?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we move in private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, you've indicated that you changed position, I believe, at the beginning of the month of June of 2002 and that you changed position within the ministry. Would you be able to say what position you went to next?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Immediately after my departure from the sector for security of the president, I was issued a decision to be deputy to the assistant to the minister for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And how long approximately, if you can recall, did you stay in that position?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I stayed in that position for about two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what position or job did you go to next?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: My next job was assistant to the director in the directorate security and counter-intelligence for operative matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you indicate, again if you can remember, how long approximately you stayed in that position?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I stayed in my position between the beginning of August 2002 and until my termination of employment with the Ministry of the Interior, which was at the beginning of January 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the previous ruling of the Chamber we'll not explore the circumstances under which he left the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, were you at some stage requested by the Ministry of the Interior to return any money or any item that you had received in the course of your employment in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: So, after the termination of my employment, I did not receive any request to return any means or instruments until a point in time, in 2006, when I received at my home address a summon for court hearing, because I had allegedly failed to return a 600 -- restore 600 dollars to the ministry of the interior, around 24.000 Macedonian dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are those proceedings ongoing, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. It is still ongoing and on the 17th of March this year we have a hearing in the Basic Court Skopje II.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps very briefly, Mr. Keskovski, if you can, could you indicate what those 600 dollars relate to?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: This 600 dollars are related to a trip to the Republic of Croatia in November 2002 when the Republic of Macedonia -- November 2000 when it initialed the stablisation and association agreement with the European Union. I, as the head of security of the president, went together to Croatia in a car as the first group that went and when returning there is a -- there was a -- the road was blocked between Nis and Skopje, because of the military activities of the army of the then Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, that was fighting with the liberation army of Presevo, Medvedje and Bujanovac, so the road was blocked and we needed to go to the Republic of Bulgaria. To be able then to reach Macedonia there were an additional 400 kilometres or something and the money was spent for that purpose and not for any personal need.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Has any other proceeding been initiated against you by the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. Not now, not ever in my life, regardless of whether it was from an official -- in my official capacity or in my capacity of an individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And before perhaps we move on to the evidence most directly relevant to this case, Mr. Keskovski. Let me ask you this: Are you in any way related to Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The Minister Boskoski was the best man at my wedding.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you say why you chose Mr. Boskoski to be your best man at your wedding?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Because of the simple reason, I wanted an honest person to be the best man at my wedding.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you continue to have friendly relationship or relations with the family of Mr. Boskoski to this day?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you feel that this relationship would impair your ability to say the truth before this Chamber, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. Since I am here to speak the truth and I declared that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you now a few questions, Mr. Keskovski, about the structure of the sector in which you worked, the sector of security of the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask the registry to bring up what is Exhibit 1D107, please. Your Honour, we also have a binder for the Judges, our colleagues and for the witness. We have been relatively modest, there is only one binder per person, and with the assistance of the usher we could distribute them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, the document which has appeared in front of you is also in your binder, under tab 2, if it is more comfortable for you to look at a paper copy.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as you can see, Mr. Keskovski, this document is the Book of Rules of organisation and operation of the ministry of the interior affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask the registry to turn to page 6 of that document. That would be 1D004397, and it would be 4375 in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, the article in question would be Article 5. Do you have that? It would be ... If you look at the numbering at the bottom of the page in your version, should be 1D00-4375.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply for identification purposes, Mr. Keskovski, is Article 5 the article of the rule book that pertains to generally the sector for security of the minister of the interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: The Article 5 pertains to the sector for security and the Article 5.1 pertains to the unit for security of the president of the Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful. You've answered my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I could ask the registry now to turn to page 1D00-4414 in the English and 1D00-4390 in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, if you turn in your version this would be the last-page-but-one in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recognise this diagram, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the organisational chart of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps with the assistance of the usher, would you be able to locate on this particular diagram the location in the structure of the sector for security? I think it is called sector for protection in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: The unit for protection of the president is within the bureau for public security. Should I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'd seek to tender this picture separately, if it's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If Your Honour prefer, we could have the English version marked if it is preferable for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the English version please be brought in. It would be page 1D00-4414.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, I apologise for asking you to do so twice, but are you able to locate the sector for protection or the sector for security in which you worked at the time on the English version?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, no problem. Let me just find it. Give me a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you perhaps locate it on the screen, Mr. Keskovski.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would seek to tender the English version instead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D315, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, I'll ask you now to turn to what is tab 3 of your binder. And this would be Rule 65 ter 1D1297.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is one of the two documents that have not been placed on our 65 ter list yet. Well, it appears not to have been uploaded yet, Your Honour. In that case we move on and we'll come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, could you tell what ministry or ministries had contributed employees to your sector, the sector of security of the president?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: The sector for security of the president was assisted by the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you explain perhaps under what circumstances members of the army or the Ministry of Defence came to operate within that sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Members of the army of the Republic of Macedonia specifically came to our sector upon the order of the president of the Republic of Macedonia after the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia commenced, based on the order of the president the group for security was reinforced by some additional 30 members from the Ministry of Defence or the army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were those individuals placed under your authority as head of the sector or were they placed under a different chain of command?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Members of the army of the Republic of Macedonia were under my direct command.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another document at this stage, Mr. Keskovski. That is Rule 65 ter 1D1138.3. And you can also find the document in English only under tab 4 of your binder. It would be tab 4, Mr. Keskovski. As you can see, this is a letter dated the 28th of July of 2005. It comes from the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, and it was sent to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal. And I would like to draw your attention to the second bulleted paragraph in the middle of the document. That would be page 1D00-9269, for the registry. Thank you very much. Mr. Keskovski, let me read to you a sentence from that particular letter. It reads as follows: "From a legal point of view the head of the presidential security unit in the Ministry of Interior has no authority over the Ministry of Defence's staff responsible for the security of the president." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And under the law of Macedonia, is that a correct position of principle?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn, please, to the next page. I'll draw your attention to the last bulleted paragraph on that document and in particular the last sentence in that document. It says that: "... Positive regulations specify that the Ministry of Interior has no competence over army staff." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again is that a position of principle that is correct under Macedonian law?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I don't believe the witness is in a position to -- to know the legal niceties of Macedonian law. I don't think that was his position. He is not called here as an expert nor is he called as a person who is necessarily familiar with Macedonian law, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I can rephrase, Your Honour. My colleague may have a point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think she does, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: She does.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, can I ask you that you in a different manner. According to your experience and your years of experience in the Ministry of the Interior, would that be a position that is consistent with your experience of the way the Ministry of Interior functioned?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But did the president have the power, if he wished, to reorganise the way in which the army and the police interacted and cooperated or was that not a possibility that was open to him at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: He could do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps focussing more specifically on your sector, the sector for security of the president, did it ever happen that the president, by an order of the president or the presidential cabinet that the decision was taken to subordinate a number of members of the army to your authority?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Upon our request, upon my request, and communication with the advisor for national security, at the beginning of the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia, we requested that the president assist us in raising the security, the protection of the president at a higher level, since at that time the president of the Republic of Macedonia is now and has ever been the supreme commander of the armed forces of the Republic of Macedonia and through his order members of the army of the Republic of Macedonia could be placed at our disposal to assist us in performing our tasks related to the president -- to the security of the president as an institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know if at any point in time an order was issued to sanction what you have just described?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, an order was issued for around 35 members of the special forces of the army of the Republic of Macedonia to join the personal security of the president of the Republic of Macedonia and under the coordination -- in coordination with the head for security of the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps, Mr. Keskovski, I will ask you now to turn to what is tab 5 of your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document is not yet uploaded in e-court and we apologise for it. We believe these two documents will be later today.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, do you have this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: For the record this is Rule 65 ter 1D1298. Is it correct that this is an order that comes from the president of the Republic of Macedonia and more specifically his cabinet? It is dated 26th February 2001 and it's to the head of the army of the Republic to the headquarters to General Colonel Jovan Andrevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct also that if you look at the contents of the document that it relates to the personal protection of the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask you to look at the last paragraph but one in this document, which starts with the words: "Furthermore, all these ... Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will just read out this sentence to you. It says this: "Furthermore, all these army of the Republic of Macedonia members, including the technical equipment, that is to say the motor vehicles, must be placed under the command of one officer that will be subordinated to President Trajkovsk, chief of security in accordance with the need to coordinate the security system." Would that document, Mr. Keskovski, be consistent with what you have recounted a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would formally seek first to -- leave to add this document to our Rule 65 ter lists and also to tender this document in evidence. As I have indicated, I believe the document would be in e-court hopefully in the course of the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any concern, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No. Not for this document, no, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Mettraux, leave will be granted. The document will also be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that would be Exhibit 1D316, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, do you know of other circumstances where it was not the army but the police that was subordinated to the army? Are you aware of any such instances?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you able, perhaps, to give examples that are known to you where this occurred?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: During the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia, there were several cases where the police was under the command of the army of the Republic of Macedonia in several actions, specifically when cleaning the Tetovo area, the Aracinovo action, the action in the Kumanovo and Lipkovo region.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you able, Mr. Keskovski, to indicate for the Chamber how you are able to say that this was the case in those particular location? How did that knowledge come to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I was personally sent to participate in all these events by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, in order to observe the situation and report or inform regarding the actions that were taking place in the field. I was present at almost all these activities that took place during the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you have just been recorded as saying that you were sent to inform, I believe you said. Who directed the request to you, who were you supposed to inform?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: As I already said, I was sent by the president of the Republic of Macedonia to the field, to inform him about the situations taking place during the actions during the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry to interrupt. Sorry to have to raise this once again, Your Honour, but this is, again, information that we didn't quite receive from my colleague either in the Rule 65 ter (G) summary or the proofing note. There's nothing in here that I see that indicates the witness was present at these actions and was sent specifically by the president to inform him of what was taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take issue with that. We have indicated yesterday following a specific request by my colleague that the witness was aware of instances where this had taken place, I believe he has mentioned one, we had mentioned three of those yesterday, the three areas or places which he had referred to us in relation to these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that accepted, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can just clarify, Your Honour, what the difficulty is. It is one thing to say in the general format that he knows of several cases where this had taken place and he lists a number of places. It's quite another to say that he was sent there by the president to inform him about what was going on in all these locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will receive this evidence, Mr. Mettraux, but if it is the case that Ms. Issa is in difficulty with the notice, it may that there will have to be some deferral of cross-examination on this issue. The need for disclosure is a need that requires a more adequate notice of something as significant as this than it appears to have been given on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we fully understand this point and I believe we sent yesterday a very large proofing note which gave a great deal of information to our colleagues about information which we believed was not already obvious from the very lengthy statement that was provided by Mr. Keskovski in relation to his expected evidence and we believe we have given a great deal of information. The question for us is how much we can then explore in evidence in chief. But we have that in mind, Your Honour, and we'll try to proceed with caution. And I see the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will have the first break now and resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and we have been able to locate the document, thanks to our colleague from the Prosecution and I'm grateful. This is Rule 65 ter 09.1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Keskovski, if it is easier for you, this is also the document that is under tab number 3 of your binder. Do you recognise this document, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know who the author of that document is?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. It is I.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you did it, didn't you, during an interview with the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you explain briefly what this diagram represents?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I can. However, if I may have a look at my drawing, the diagram that I've drawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the handmade drawing be shown to the witness, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you explain briefly, Mr. Keskovski, what this diagram represents?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is a diagram of the manner of organisation which is presented in diagram form as to how the security services of the president of the Republic, Mr. Boris Trajkovski, functioned while I was head of his security.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would cover the period of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you perhaps briefly describe the subsectors which made up your -- the security sector of the president?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: The security section for the president was reformed in the course of 2000, following the suggestions of officers of the US Secret Service who were in the Republic of Macedonia in 2000. We had two professional training with them related to providing security for high officials, and for protection operations for VIPs and by the counter-intelligence training group of the US. This is a diagram made on the basis of the consultations we had with them, in the course of 2000 and it is organised in the following manner. At the top, we have the chief of security. Further down in the diagram are the two deputies, members of the Ministry of Interior. On the right side of the diagram is the assistant or so to say my deputy from the army of the Republic of Macedonia. Vertically under my position, the diagram branches into several sections or units, the section for the personal security of the president, the physical security, then the second advance section, then the third drivers section, the fourth is the section for the protection of the family, and the fifth is the section of 24-hour duty, in front of and in the cabinet of the president of the Republic of Macedonia. The diagram on the right-hand side under the ARM assistant branches out into three different units: The SWAT unit, a snipers team for anti-sniper activity, and the third are the guards at the residence of the president of the Republic of Macedonia. Further down, at the lowest level of this diagram, we can see that the personal security has four shifts, which include an eight-hour shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's stop there for just a minute, Mr. Keskovski. There's a number of questions I would like to ask you at this stage. You've indicated that there was an army assistant which headed three different department or subsectors and what I would like to ask you is apart from the members of the army in those three subsectors, SWAT, sniper and guard, were members of the Ministry of Defence also included in the other subsectors in your section or sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to present this structure later, but since you ask, as it was written in the document which you showed me with the president's order, ten of the members of the special units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia were also in the personal -- were engaged in the personal security of the president of the Republic in these four shifts and, in part, in the advance section which was part of the president security, as civilians. As civilians. The persons shown on the right-hand side of the diagram were in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And by -- as civilians you mean that they were wearing civilian clothes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at the middle right-hand side of the document. There is an arrow which lead to the name of Johan Tarculovski. Could you state what you were indicating with that arrow and the name of Mr. Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, I was requested by the investigator to draw the diagram of the section and to mark the position of Mr. Johan Tarculovski and where he carried out his tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps to assist us, Mr. Keskovski, are you able to read the marking that is made within the square to which the arrow has been linked?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: It reads "first lady."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was that the section to which Mr. Tarculovski worked at that time, including in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps to ask you about your own position. What was your position on that diagram at the time, in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I was the chief of the sector -- or the section for security of the president, which is at the upper most part of this diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'd seek to tender this document. I'm told it's also been uploaded in another format but this is in effect the same document. We will have to seek leave as well to add it to our 65 ter. This was the second document that did not appear on our 65 ter list and perhaps for Your Honours' full information this document was annexed as annex B, I believe, to the OTP statement taken by the Prosecutor of Mr. Keskovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Leave to add to the list will be granted and it will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that would be Exhibit 1D317, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, going out of this structure and into the Ministry of Interior, could you tell who was your immediate superior at the time, in August of 2001? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: In August 2001, my direct superior was Mr. Gacovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall perhaps what the position or the title that Mr. Gacovski had at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. He was assistant to the minister for security of persons and facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know who appointed him or who selected him for that position?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. He was appointed by the government of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you receive orders or instructions in relation to the functioning and the work of your sector from Mr. Gacovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you ever report to Mr. Gacovski about the activities of your sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In August of 2001, do you recall who would have been the superior of Mr. Gacovski in the structure of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This was the director for public security, Mr. Goran Mitevski and the minister of the interior, Mr. Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you first then about Mr. Mitevski, if I may. Did you receive orders or instructions from Mr. Mitevski in August of 2001 or early, or later, for that matter, in relation to the work and functioning of your sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And turning now to the minister and I will ask you about the two ministers. Did you ever receive any orders from Minister Dimovska or her successor, Mr. Boskoski, about the work of your sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Minister Dimovska requested once that I carry out an order, while Mr. Boskoski never issued an order to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps I'll ask you, can you recall what that order of Minister Dimovska was?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: It was at the beginning of 2000 when Ms. Dimovska was appointed minister of the interior. She called me in her cabinet and her office and issued me an order to submit reports on the work of the section on security of the president of the Republic of Macedonia with reports on movements, contacts, and meetings that were held in the office of the president of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you carry out that order?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: At that very meeting, I told the minister of the interior that I would have to speak personally to President Trajkovski about this order. After my talk with him, he issued an order to me not to act on the order of the minister, not to send reports regarding his work in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And which of the two orders did you obey, Mr. Keskovski, the order of Ms. Dimovska or the order of the president?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: As I already said, I carried out the order of the president of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the course of your work, the work of your sector that is, did you at any time receive orders from the president?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. On a daily basis, I received various orders from the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you receive orders from anyone else in relation to the work and activities of your sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me go back to the internal functioning of your sector. We've seen a diagram or sort of map of that sector. I'd like to ask you and you have already explained on whose advice you had set it up in that fashion. But could you say who was responsible to decide on the internal functioning and structuring of your sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And who was responsible to decide on the distribution of tasks, let's say who was to do what within that section or sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the registry please bring up what is Rule 65 ter 1D1138.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Keskovski, this would be under tab 4 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd ask the registry once again to go to page 1D00-9269, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, as you will see, this is the same letter as I showed a little bit earlier. But I'd like this time for you to locate the third bulleted paragraph in that document. And I think that would be a bit further down the page in the English. Thank you. There is -- the second sentence of that paragraph, Mr. Keskovski, reads as follows, and I will read it out for in the English language. It says: "The internal organisation of the unit's work and the allocation of particular tasks fell under the competence of the unit's head." Would that statement be consistent with what you've said a moment ago, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at the time when you acted as head or chief of the sector for security of the president, did you regard the president as your superior?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were there any times or occasions when the president would give direct orders to yourself or to members of your sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: On a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Once again, Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting and rising, but we've heard some quite extensive evidence regarding orders given by the president to the witness and now he is talking about orders given to others by the president. None of this material appears in the proofing note nor in the Rule 65 ter (G) summary. So once again we're in a position where we have not had adequate notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll take issue with the suggestions of our colleague that they don't have adequate notice of this matter. There is extensive discussion in the statement of Mr. Keskovski of the organisation of the work, of the structure, of the people that were mentioned, of who was giving order to whom, of the policy on hiring, the policy on all sorts of matter, Your Honour, that relates to the functioning of the sector in question, including as we've indicated the diagram which was prepared by the witness. It seems hard to believe that the Prosecution would be taken aback by questions which are being asked, Your Honour, about the way in which this department or this sector was functioning. We understand it to have been one of the many purpose and reason for the calling of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, is there anything further?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it is one thing to address matters relating to the structure of the sector and how it was structured within the Ministry of Interior, for example, and that of course is in the statement. But the critical point relating to the issue of orders and the extent of those orders and perhaps the content of the orders, which I anticipate, or I'm guessing we may get to, there is nothing about that in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, perhaps briefly I will indicate that at paragraph 5 of yesterday's proofing note we indicated, among other things, that concerning the role of the president vis-a-vis the police, Mr. Keskovski was a witness to several instances when the president gave orders directly to members of the police (and other members of the Ministry of Interior, including members of his sector and to the minister himself).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, I apologise. When you received such orders from the president, would you inform the hierarchy in the Ministry of Interior that you had received such orders?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to something slightly different, which is the composition, if you want, of your sector and questions of hiring or taking people into this sector. Did the president ever give you the name or names of persons whom he wished to be taken in your sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, in continuity.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did that include members of his family, for instance?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have an example to give of other people that were close to him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. His nephew was employed in the sector for securing of the president in 1994 at the request of the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did the president made other requests that you can recall about particular -- particular person whom he wished --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: If you will allow me, in the interpretation it is stated 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the correct date was, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. Are you aware of any other cases where the president requested or demanded that a particular person should join the sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: As I already said, this happened in continuity. At the request of the president, seven to eight persons were encompassed. Some were taken from outside, some were transferred from within, from the Ministry of Interior, and from the army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did that include any person that were or could be seen as close from the president such as fellow church-goers, neighbours, friends, family members? Any sort of person of that sort that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. An acquaintance from his church, Mr. Tadues, was employed. He came from the outside. He was not employed, that is to say, at the Ministry of Interior so he was directly employed in our sector. Then an employee from the police was transferred at the request of the president in our section. He was neighbour of the president. Then Mr. Tarculovski was engaged at the request of the president personally. Mr. Stojkov, Goran was employed from the outside at the personal request of the president, and the commander engaged from the army of the Republic of Macedonia in 2001 with an order of the president and he was his close neighbour from Strumice. He was appointed as my assistant. At that time he was engaged in the army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me then ask you a follow-up question about the request of the president to have Mr. Tarculovski join the sector. Do you remember when that was approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: This was in the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall or recount the circumstances under which the president requested of you that you should take Mr. Tarculovski in the sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: The president did not request of me; rather, he ordered me to have Mr. Tarculovski transferred from the sector of security for the prime minister to our services, that is to say, the personal security of the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did the president provide any explanation for his order to you to take Mr. Tarculovski to the sector? Did he tell you why he wanted him to join?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: During one visit to the office of the prime minister, Mr. Tarculovski was working in the reception unit, and the president noticed him then. He asked him why he was where he was, and he responded that this was his work post now. The president ordered me to immediately transfer him under any circumstances since they knew each other for over five years and Mr. Tarculovski had worked at the reception desk of the political party of VRMO-DPMNE, the party where Boris Trajkovski was a member of the executive committee; therefore, they had known each other well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just to clarify this. Is it your understanding and as far as you can tell, is that how Mr. Tarculovski and President Trajkovski came to know each other? Is that through the political activities of both? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: One can say this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps to complete this issue of the hiring. In your experience, did Minister Boskoski in any way influence the selection of employees in your sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now, you've explained earlier that within your sector there were a number of subsectors and we've seen what they are. I'd like to ask you who decided on which particular member of your sector would go into what particular subsector. Who would decide that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you sometimes consult with the president about these matters?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. He usually had his wishes and orders regarding who among the members of the security of the president would take which positions and also who would be removed from the security.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did he ever make any particular suggestions, recommendations or order, in whatever form, in relation to the sector that was dealing with the security of the family, the first lady and the children?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. I wasn't very clear. Did the president made any suggestions about what members of your sector should be assigned to the subsector that was dealing with the security of his family?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did he make any particular suggestion as to the assignment of Mr. Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The president personally appointed, if I may say so, he nominated for the appointment all security members that were working on the security of the first lady and the security of -- of president's children. All those inspectors were the individuals that the president hand-picked, since he believed that this sensitive post should be occupied by individuals that he knew well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And following on this, did you ever see the president with Mr. -- with President Trajkovski. I'm sorry, did you ever see Mr. Tarculovski with the President Trajkovski during his time in your sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you able to quantify the number of time which you might have seen the two of them together during that period?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Many times. I couldn't give you a precise number.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you also sometimes see Mr. Tarculovski at the house of the president, or did that never happen?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Tarculovski, when performing his duties, was regularly present there, and I have seen him several times in the living-room of the president, in his residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this may be a difficult question, but as far as you could tell, would it appear that Mr. Tarculovski was a person that the president trusted?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Judging by the communication manner and also the answer to your previous question, I came to the living-room of the presidential residence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the only individuals personally invited by the president of the Republic of Macedonia or his wife, the first lady had access to the living-room of the president.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: As far as I remember, and I know that -- I think I know well that I only had access to the private residential parts of the residence of the president, in addition to Mr. Tarculovski, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So would that suggest a particular level of trust vis-a-vis the president?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour. I'm objecting to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's incredibly leading on a fairly important point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Technically so. The answer is virtually self-evident though. Mr. Mettraux, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: May I ask the question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, would that suggest a particular level of trust vis-a-vis the president? And I was talking of the level of trust between Mr. Tarculovski and the president.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe that from everything that I said thus far, it is evident that Mr. Tarculovski was one of the members of the security sector that enjoyed high confidence of the President Trajkovski and the first lady, Mrs. Vilma Trajkovska.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me ask you about something slightly different now, Mr. Keskovski, and that relates to the means of communications that were at the disposal of your sector at the time. Could you say what means of communication or what facilities you used to communicate between the various members of your sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: The communication between the members of the sector for security of the president went via several instruments, land line, special telephone network, communication network, radio station, Motorola, with its own channel, and mobile phones that were available at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And asking specifically about yourself, Mr. Keskovski, do you recall how many mobile phones you had or used in August of 2001, if more than one?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: I had two all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you remember - I know it's quite some time now - are you able to recall perhaps what numbers you might have used during that time, August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, those were 070344044 and I believe I had another phone number which was 358178. And the prefix is the same, 070.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know a number 070360000? Are you familiar with this number?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. That was my number as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps I'll ask the registry to bring up what is Rule 65 ter 1D1138.2, please. That would be page 1D00-9263.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, this is a list of telephone numbers that was provided at some point by the Ministry of Interior to the Office of the Prosecutor and it contains a number of telephone numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask the registry to go to the second page of that document, please. I apologise --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Where do I find it here?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. This is tab 6 bis, please. 6 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me ask you this as a general question first, Mr. Keskovski. How did it work in practice the mobile phones that were given to your sector? Were they given to you or were they given to individual members or did that vary? How did it work?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Most of the phone numbers were registered in my name but there were also phone numbers that were registered in the names of other individuals from the sector for security of the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if I ask you to look down that list of number, Mr. Keskovski, under number 25 and 26. There are two different telephone numbers which are 070279418 and 070279419 and they are registered under your name. Are you able to say who, if you can recall, used those numbers in August of 2001? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: These numbers, or most of them, were numbers used by the entire group for security of the president and across various units of that we already defined on the diagram and that they were on a permanent rotation or shifting. I really couldn't remember all persons who used those numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, can we please look at the next page, please. First I'll ask to you look perhaps at number 34. There's a number and a person by the name of Aco Mladenov. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you able to say what job or function or role Mr. Mladenov had in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Mladenov, Aco, was the personal driver of the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Mr. Boris Trajkovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can now look further down the page under number 50 there's another number, it's 070358178, and it's again under your name. Is it one of the numbers that you've given a moment ago as one of those numbers which you used in that period?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. And as far as I can remember, that's one of the numbers that I have used.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did the president sometimes use the phones of his body-guards or security people, including yours?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. That happened every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps I should have been more precise in my question. Did you ever use your mobile phone?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, always. And it happened every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did he sometime used the telephone number, or the phone, I should say, of other members of the security sector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, I'd like to read to you a passage from the transcript of this trial. It's at page 5550 and the evidence was given by Mr. Zoran Trajkovski. First I should ask you this: Do you know who Mr. Zoran Trajkovski is?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that he is the head of security for Mr. Minister, Ljube Boskoski. At that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at page 5550 he said this, the question was: "And this happened at times when the president would ask for the minister or when the minister had to call in to the president. Is it correct?"

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: "Well, yes. Our practice was that one of the person who took care of his security had the mobile phone, had his mobile phone so when the president or the prime minister called the minister would speak of this -- with these persons. Oftentimes Keskovski, Zlatko, yes, requested the minister when the president had done so," and there's a further question. "That would in fact be my next question to you. It was usual practice that the minister or the president or the prime minister not have their mobile phone on their person but that they be with their security and through the security the other security will be contacted or directly the president or the minister. Is that correct?" And the answer of Mr. Trajkovski was: "Yes, this is correct." Would that description given by Mr. Trajkovski be consistent with your experience as the chief of security of the president of the Republic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. That was the mode of communication between the institutions when they're outside of their cabinets.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And following on that, then, were there cases when people would call your mobile phone or your phone number with a view to communicate with the president?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: My mobile phone number was the main communication channel for the president when he was outside of his cabinet, of his office. My phone number would be called by an entire spectrum of persons ranging from private acquaintances of the president and even public representatives, including international organisations, including presidents of states, ministers for internal affairs or foreign affairs of other states, NATO Secretary-General and many, many other individuals who wanted to speak to President Trajkovski personally, because in their communication he always left my phone number as his direct contact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would that happen? Have you been a witness to the president giving orders on the phone?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We'll come back perhaps to that a bit later, Mr. Keskovski. But I'd like to ask you about a very specific order. Were you ever the witness of Mr. Trajkovski, President Trajkovski, giving an order to Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall any particular instance or incident when that happened?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I recall the event related to cease-fire during the army action that involved the police as well at Aracinovo. I think that -- or as far as I remember, it was on the 23rd or 24th of June, 2001. The president called me to his office, and Mr. Ambassador was there, Peter Feith. At that moment the ambassador was the acting ambassador of NATO to the Republic of Macedonia. He asked me to give him my phone and he asked me to establish immediately the contact with Mr. Ljube Boskoski, so I did call Boskoski's number and I gave the phone to the president. He told the minister to immediately, at this very moment, terminate any activity related to the action that was taking place on the territory of Aracinovo village near Skopje, and that I was personally in charge to take the ambassador to the Hotel Bellevue for a meeting with the minister, Ljube Boskoski, head of the General Staff, and the defence minister, Mr. Buckovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, as a preliminary matter --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: That was one such example. The next time I could remember this happened was precisely on the date 25th of June, 2001, and I can be specific about it because this is the birth date of the late president, Trajkovski. There was unrest in front of the parliament building. There was a meeting inside the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia between the president of the state, prime minister, and all political parties that were involved or represented in the parliament. Since I, learning what the situation was outside in front of the parliament building, I suggested to the president that this meeting should be terminated due to security reasons. The president together with the prime minister agreed. They terminated the meeting and went towards the cabinet together with me, towards the cabinet of the president of the Republic of Macedonia and then from the windows they were observing the development of the situation in front of the parliament building, the that were taking place there, that is. He told me that I should phone the minister immediately and I phoned the minister. He spoke to him personally and ordered the minister of the interior to come immediately in front of the parliament building and calm the already outraged crowd down and to resolve the situation around the parliament and the unrest in front of the parliament building.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Going back for a minute to the first example that you gave, that of Aracinovo. Do you know whether the police actually pulled out as ordered by the president?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. All activities related to the action in Aracinovo were terminated immediately. Both the police units and the army units terminated the activities because it was actually an action of the army of the Republic of Macedonia fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And let me perhaps read another passage from the transcript on that point. This is from page 9118, it's the 7th of February of 2008, and it's from a Defence witness, who said this, Mr. Keskovski. He said: "For clarification, immediately in the days before, actually, the Ministry of Interior took action to seize control over the village of Aracinovo and had clashes with the terrorists who were located there at that time. When the clashes started an order was issued. I believe that it was an order issued by the president, the late president of the state and probably pressured by the international community" -- "international public." I apologise. Would that statement, namely that the order had come from the president, be consistent with what you've just said, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the registry please bring what is now admitted as Exhibit 1D211.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, this would be under tab 14, 1-4, of your binder if it is more practical.
